user: And I still have time to file, right?
answer:
It depends on the transaction and the reason code, because each reason has its own window counted from the transaction date. Using today's date of **15 September 2026** from your limit data:

| Transaction | Reason code | Window | Days elapsed | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TX-0401 (20 Jul, EUR 240) | duplicate_charge | 60 days | 57 | Open, about 3 days left |
| TX-0402 (14 Jul, EUR 240) | duplicate_charge | 60 days | 63 | Closed |
| Either (fraud_card_not_present) | fraud_card_not_present | 120 days | 57 or 63 | Open |
| Either (goods_not_received or service_not_rendered) | goods_not_received / service_not_rendered | 90 days | 57 or 63 | Open |
| Either (unauthorized_debit) | unauthorized_debit | 56 days | 57 or 63 | Closed |

So if you were charged twice, **TX-0401 is the only one still within the duplicate-charge window**, and it closes in about 3 days. If the purchase was never received or the charge was unauthorised, you have more time, but the unauthorised-debit window has already closed. For that case, fraud_card_not_present may still apply.

Tell me which transaction and what happened, and I'll check eligibility before anything is filed. If the duplicate-charge window matters to you, I'd act soon.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Limit operations
## Window definition
Limits are tracked on calendar days, not business days. The daily window runs
from 00:00 to 23:59 CET.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Glossary
## Chargeback window
The number of days, counted from the transaction date, during which a dispute
may be raised under a given reason code.
